title: Count Number of Homogenous Substrings
summary: For a given string, count the number of contiguous substrings where all characters are identical, then return this count modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: For a given string, count the number of contiguous substrings where all characters are identical, then return this count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: A substring is homogeneous when every character in it is the same.
Count all nonempty homogeneous substrings by position, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: A run of length r contributes r substrings ending at its newest character.
Track the current equal-character suffix length and add it at every position.
Reset run to one on a character change; otherwise increment it; reduce the total modulo M.
Every homogeneous substring is uniquely identified by its ending position and one of the current run-length starting points.
editorial: Every homogeneous substring is uniquely identified by its ending position and one of the current run-length starting points.

Each one-character substring is homogeneous, giving two.
